issue.title: Non-atomic portfolio cache write causes json.JSONDecodeError under concurrent hooks
issue.actual_behavior: _write_cache() in src/chip_labs/hooks.py (lines 224-264) uses direct cache_file.write_text() which is not atomic. Concurrent SessionStart and PreToolUse hooks can read a partially-written JSON cache file, triggering json.JSONDecodeError and falling back to the expensive full V3 deep eval load (~3s per chip). The same non-atomic pattern exists in _write_session_domain() (lines 164-178).
issue.expected_behavior: Cache writes should be atomic so concurrent readers always see either the complete old file or the complete new file, never a partial/corrupt write. The _write_session_domain() function should also use atomic writes.
repro_steps: Open src/chip_labs/hooks.py and examine _write_cache() around lines 224-264.
Note that cache_file.write_text() performs a non-atomic open+write+close sequence.
When a SessionStart hook is writing the cache and a PreToolUse hook reads it concurrently, the reader can observe partial JSON.
This triggers json.JSONDecodeError in _load_from_cache(), causing an expensive fallback to full portfolio load.
The same pattern exists in _write_session_domain() at lines 164-178.
issue.affected_workflow: Portfolio cache read/write during concurrent hook invocations

evidence.before_after_proof: Before: _write_cache() uses cache_file.write_text(json.dumps(...)) directly (non-atomic). _write_session_domain() uses _SESSION_DOMAIN_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(...)) directly (non-atomic). After: Both functions call _atomic_write_json() which uses tempfile.mkstemp() + os.fdopen() + os.replace() for atomic rename. Temp file is cleaned up on any failure. Both functions maintain identical serialization logic and error handling.

proposed_fix.approach: Add a _atomic_write_json() helper that writes JSON to a tempfile via tempfile.mkstemp() then atomically renames it to the target via os.replace(). Update _write_cache() and _write_session_domain() to use this helper instead of direct write_text(). Temp file cleanup is guaranteed on failure via BaseException handler.
proposed_fix.tests_or_smoke: Existing tests pass unchanged. The fix only changes the write mechanism (atomic vs non-atomic). The serialized content and error handling are identical. os.replace() is atomic on POSIX and effectively atomic on Windows.

review_claim.duplicate_notes: No existing PR addresses atomic cache writes in hooks.py. Other PRs in the repo address different bugs (KeyError, score-or-chain, code injection, partial state, etc.). The fix/gap-analyzer-atomic-write branch addresses atomic writes in a different file (gap_analyzer), not in hooks.py.
review_claim.risk_notes: Low risk. The fix only changes the write mechanism. Serialized content is identical. os.replace() is a well-established atomic write pattern. Temp file cleanup is guaranteed. No behavioral change on the happy path.
